scenes.line1: How do you secure a 3-tier app?
scenes.say: You’ll get asked this a lot: how do you design a secure, classic three-tier deployment in the cloud?

rows.b: Private subnet, app VMs or AKS

scenes.say: Picture three layers: web, app, and data. Each lives in its own subnet. The web tier faces the world, the app tier runs your logic, and the data tier holds your database, locked down tight.

scenes.label: NSGs
scenes.sub: Allow only needed ports between tiers; deny all else.
scenes.say: Network security groups only allow the traffic you need. For example, web to app on port eighty eighty, app to data on fourteen thirty-three. Everything else is blocked.

scenes.label: Private
scenes.sub: Private endpoints keep your database off the public net.
scenes.say: Private endpoints make sure your database never touches the public internet. Only the app tier can reach it.

scenes.question: What if you skip availability zones?
scenes.right: Without zones, a datacenter outage can take down your whole app.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: if you only use availability sets, you’re still at risk if a whole datacenter goes down. Always spread your web and app VMs across zones.
